summary: F1 is fixed: a damaged or unreadable channel file now falls back to production and is logged. The new temp tests check the channel-to-config mapping and the update repository wiring with real assertions. I accept the reason for leaving main.ts untested: importing it starts the app as a side effect. ControlPlaneAuth.start's changed lines (67, 69) remain uncovered and have no exemption, although a small temp test with a mocked `electron` can check them easily.

findings.body: The main.ts exemption is accepted: importing main.ts starts the app as a side effect, so it cannot load under vitest. Lines 67 and 69 of `ControlPlaneAuth.start` are still uncovered and have no exemption. Taking the session file from `sessionPath` instead of `dataDir/control-plane-session` is what keeps the staging and production sign-ins apart. Add a temp test that mocks `electron`'s `safeStorage` (encrypt/decrypt as identity, `isAsyncEncryptionAvailable` resolving true) and starts `ControlPlaneAuth` with a custom `sessionPath`. It should check that the token stored at that path is used, for example through the bearer token on the request that `getSession` or `getWorkspaceConnection` makes, and that a session at the default `control-plane-session` path is not read.

testRequests.target: apps/electron/src/main/auth/ControlPlaneAuth.ts:67-69 — ControlPlaneAuth.start reads the session token from ctx.sessionPath
testRequests.rationale: These changed lines are uncovered and not exempt, and they carry the per-channel session separation.
